Design screen layouts and screen flows for the identified objects. This provides visualization of screen layouts and screen flows of the proposed graphical user interface (GUI) so that the stakeholders can visualize and confirm the proposed screen flow and navigation. This helps in early detection of any gaps in expectations that should be taken into consideration.

Design the screen layout and flows by:

  • Creating solution screen layouts and screen flows for identified requirements
  • Conducting reviews of screen layouts and screen flows with stakeholders and gather their inputs
  • Reworking any user interface requirements based on stakeholder feedback
  • Confirming review of final screen layouts and screen flows after rework

Make sure stakeholders are involved in order to validate and confirm the proposed solution screen layout and screen flows.

Element.Name: Establish application error handling approach
Element.copyright:
© 2012, 2022 EYGM Limited. All Rights Reserved.
Privacy Notice

Powered by Global Methods in conjunction with Consulting Methods
Element.attribute:
Define the design approach that should be followed for capturing, reporting and resolving errors within applications (e.g., interface and data transfer failures). The standards and guidelines should address the various categories of errors and define appropriate resolution paths for each.

In order to capture, report and resolve package application errors:

  • Define error categories and types of errors within each category
  • Define error conditions and resolution options
  • Define error and process log
  • Define reconciliation report (and distribution list)
  • Define post execution notification mechanism
  • Define restart/recovery procedure
  • Include monitoring/automated alert notifications where relevant and/or possible

The error handling strategy is most commonly identified as relevant for interface scenarios to track failures of data transfers, but it is also relevant for other development (coding) scenarios. The development standards should also contain guidance on error handling for each development object. Those standards should align with the overall error handling strategy.

The error handling framework should categorize the errors (business, technical, miscellaneous) and provide resolution paths for the various categories:

  • Business errors include logic, data format, or data conversion errors
  • Technical errors include communication (dropped database connections, unavailability of systems) or infrastructure errors (network availability or performance, client library availability, disk usage)
  • Miscellaneous errors include invalid logon credentials, scheduling, and time constraints or threshold errors
